opportunities.title: Young Women in Mind 2026-2028
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charity (for at least three years) already delivering therapeutic mental health services; mental health charity with clear youth and mental health mission and annual income of £750,000+, OR specialist charity led by and for women and girls with clear mental health mission, experience delivering services to under 18s, and annual income of £350,000+. Must operate in Northern Ireland, Scotland, or the English regions North East, North West, Yorkshire and Humber, the Midlands (UK-wide/England-wide organisations welcome).
opportunities.summary: Collaborative funding programme with the Prudence Trust and Julia Rausing Trust to support charities providing gender-specific therapeutic mental health support for girls and young women aged 14-25 in the UK, strengthening and scaling services. £5 million invested over three years (2026-2028).

opportunities.title: Historic Buildings and Structures (Preservation and Conservation grants)

amount.raw: Generally £1,000 to £30,000 (average approx. £15,000). Sometimes larger sums are considered.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, organisations with exempt charitable status, recognised public bodies, Community Benefit Societies, and Community Interest Companies (CIC) limited by guarantee. Work must be UK based, not complete, and focus on a listed building or structure.
opportunities.summary: Funds the preservation and repair of listed historic buildings, structures and architectural features, with special consideration for sustainable conservation and re-use of historic buildings at risk and of outstanding importance. Rolling stage-one applications; stage-two above £5,000 considered quarterly.

opportunities.title: Places of worship (Preservation and Conservation grants)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Anglican churches apply via the ChurchCare conservation grants scheme (part-funded by the Pilgrim Trust); all other denominations, faiths and cathedrals may apply directly. Applications for conservation of historic interiors and historic objects in places of worship open for regular worship.
opportunities.summary: Funds conservation of historic interiors and historic objects in listed places of worship open for regular worship, including bells, books and manuscripts, clocks, decorative plasterwork, metalwork and church plate, monuments, organs, paintings, stained glass, textiles, timberwork, wall paintings and historic structures in churchyards, plus commissioning of conservation reports.

opportunities.title: Conservation of Cultural Heritage (Preservation and Conservation grants)
opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK registered charities, organisations with exempt charitable status, recognised public bodies, Community Benefit Societies, and Community Interest Companies (CIC) limited by guarantee. Applicants must not be eligible for the grant programmes run by AIM and NMCT. Work must be UK based and not complete.
opportunities.summary: Funds the conservation of culturally and historically significant collections and objects, including works of art, books, significant ephemera, artefacts and archives, carried out by an accredited conservator and informed by a conservation report, enabling greater public access.
